items.stimulus: Cover crops planted after harvest are widely credited with returning nitrogen to the soil, but few studies have followed that nitrogen into the next season's crop. items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: "Measured" is a verb, and its object is the pair of clauses "how much nitrogen each cover crop released and how much of it the following corn crop actually absorbed". A verb and its object are never separated by punctuation. The comma after "plots" ends the introductory phrase, and it does not call for another mark later.

A.why: The long object made you want a pause after the verb. A comma never separates a verb from its object, even when the object is a long "how" clause.

B.why: You saw two "how" clauses and treated them like a list a colon introduces. But a colon needs a complete sentence before it, and "agronomists... measured" is unfinished without its object.

C.why: A single dash follows the same rule as a colon: the text before it must be a complete sentence, and it is not. The dash also separates "measured" from its object.
